tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[Dichotomy: uniform backward parabolic neighborhood or a canonical neighborhood] After passing to a subsequence, either for every $A$ there are $D(A),t(A)>0$ such that $P(\widetilde x_a,0,A,-t(A))$ exists with $|\Rm |\leq D(A)$, or every $x_a$ has a strong $(C,\epsilon )$-canonical neighborhood. \end{claim}

Proof

\sketch ↗ claim:curvature-bound-along-backward-flow-lines ↗ lem:std-cap-canonical-neighborhood If a uniform backward parabolic neighborhood exists, Claim 2 supplies the curvature bound. Otherwise a bounded-radius ball contains a flow line reaching a surgery cap in arbitrarily short time; the same claim bounds its curvature, and Lemma 1 gives a canonical neighborhood.

□
